rejected_findings.issue: Pass-2 loudnorm re-encodes audio without -shortest; if the 16:9 audio stream is longer than the video (common with AAC priming/padding), the corrected final's duration grows, breaking A/V sync at the tail and the 9:16 mux inherits it
rejected_findings.fix: Add -shortest (or -t = source duration) to the pass-2 encode and the 9:16 mux; assert duration delta < 1 frame after correction

rejected_findings.issue: The regex only matches a JSON object containing input_i; if ffmpeg's stderr contains another JSON blob first (e.g. from a prior -af or banner), the wrong blob is parsed; also normalization_type is returned as a string while all other keys are floats, so callers comparing it numerically will fail
rejected_findings.fix: Parse the LAST match (re.findall + [-1]) and validate required keys (input_i, input_tp, input_lra, input_thresh, target_offset) exist before returning

rejected_findings.issue: test_a_pair_within_tolerance_is_never_rewritten does not test what it claims: it calls correct_finals twice on the SAME pair, so the second call's 'none: within tolerance' only proves the first call's correction worked, not that an in-tolerance pair is skipped; the fixture never produces a genuinely in-tolerance (between -14.5 and -13.5) but uncorrected pair
rejected_findings.evidence: f16, f9 = make_pair(self.d, 0.03); LD.correct_finals(f16, f9)  # now at the target; s16, s9 = sha(f16), sha(f9); rec = LD.correct_finals(f16, f9)
rejected_findings.fix: Build a second pair with a volume chosen so its measured input_i lands within [-14.5, -13.5] without any prior correction, then assert action == 'none: within tolerance' and unchanged hashes on that fresh pair
